claims: Creator has been a software developer for five years
Level 1 'model routing': Claude for code, ChatGPT for brainstorming, Gemini for research
Level 2 'model chaining': run models in sequence, e.g. Gemini researches branding -> ChatGPT makes a brand-kit image -> Claude builds the site; 'puts you ahead of 90% of people'
Level 3 'multi-model council': run several models in parallel on the same task, then have them review and rank each other to produce a final output; 'how the top 1% use AI'
Promises setup 'in less than 60 seconds' but shows only diagrams
how_to_steps: Level 1: pick the model per task type (code -> Claude, brainstorm -> ChatGPT, research -> Gemini)
Level 2: chain outputs — Gemini research -> ChatGPT brand kit (image) -> Claude code -> final site
Level 3: send the same prompt to Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude in parallel -> 'Council Review' step where they rank each other -> final output
on_screen_only: Title card 'Why Claude IS NOT Better than ChatGPT' (Claude vs ChatGPT logos)
Slides styled 'Claude Editorial Spark': 'Multi Model Chaining — One system. Three levels. Better outputs.' with a 'Multi Model Orchestrator' (Route/Chain/Council) node
Level 1 slide 'Model Routing — Pick the best model for the task' (Code->Claude, Brainstorm->ChatGPT, Research->Gemini, 'Beginner mode')
Level 2 slide 'Model Chaining — Run models in sequence' ('Ahead of 90%'); flow: Task/Prompt -> 1 Gemini Research branding -> 2 ChatGPT Create brand kit -> 3 Claude Build site -> Final Site
Level 3 slide 'Multi Model Council — Run models in parallel, then review the best answer' ('Top 1%'): Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude -> Council Review -> Final Output

relevance.why: Conceptual only; the council idea maps to things already available (Claude Code subagents, LLM-as-judge) but the video gives no tooling, prompts or evidence.

implement_score.why: A 'council' is cheap to prototype with Claude Code subagents or a few API calls plus a judge prompt, but this video adds nothing beyond the name; only do it for high-stakes decisions where a second opinion is worth the token cost.

verify: Is there any evidence that parallel multi-model councils beat a single strong model plus self-review for coding tasks?
Cost: three models in parallel plus a ranking pass roughly 4x the tokens per task
What orchestration tool does the creator actually use (none shown)?
